The module has correctness bugs in stock accounting, several panic and overflow paths, three `unsafe` blocks that are undefined behavior on realistic inputs, and a lock-order deadlock in `Service`.

### Stock accounting

`receive` always `insert`s a brand-new `Item`. For an existing SKU that drops the previous `on_hand`, `reserved`, name, and price. The comment says a repeat receipt adds units. Any `Service` hold on that SKU is then pointing at a reservation that no longer exists.

`release` uses `saturating_sub` and returns `Ok` when `qty` is larger than `reserved`, so extra releases succeed and eat other reservations.

`record_loss` does `on_hand -= lost` with no check. In debug that panics when `lost > on_hand`; in release it wraps. A loss that is within `on_hand` but larger than unreserved stock leaves `reserved > on_hand`.

`available` is `on_hand - reserved`, so once that invariant breaks it panics in debug and wraps in release. `reserve` and `low_stock` both call it.

`ship` checks `qty` against `reserved` only, then does `on_hand -= qty`. If losses have already pulled `on_hand` below `reserved`, that subtraction panics or wraps.

`total_value` does `on_hand as u64 * price_cents` and then `sum()`. Either the multiply or the sum overflows `u64` (debug panic, release wrap), so the reported value is wrong for large prices or large catalogs.

### Panics in the helpers

`moving_average` `assert`s `window > 0`, so a zero window panics instead of returning an error.

`deltas` loops `i` over `0..prices.len()` and reads `prices[i + 1]`. Any non-empty slice panics on the last index. The intended length is `prices.len() - 1`, which the `with_capacity` call already uses. The subtraction is also plain `i64` arithmetic, so values such as `i64::MAX - i64::MIN` panic in debug and wrap in release.

### Undefined behavior

`SlotTable::lookup` calls `get_unchecked` on a slot taken from a scanner message. An out-of-range index is undefined behavior, not a bounds error.

`append_batch` takes `buf.as_ptr().wrapping_add(start)` and then `extend_from_slice`s the rest of the batch. Extension can reallocate and free that allocation. The later `unsafe { *first }` is a use-after-free. `head` is already a `Copy` value, so the pointer is unnecessary.

`decode` builds the name with `str::from_utf8_unchecked` on bytes from the network. Invalid UTF-8 is undefined behavior.

### Codec

`encode` stores `name.len() as u8`. A name longer than 255 bytes is written in full with a truncated length. `decode` then treats the wrong slice as the name and the following name bytes as `sku` and `qty`. If that cut splits a multibyte character, the unchecked UTF-8 read is also undefined behavior for output this encoder produced.

### `Service` concurrency and holds

`place_hold` and `sweep_expired` lock `warehouse` and then `holds`. `confirm` locks `holds` and then `warehouse`. One thread in `confirm` and another in `place_hold` or `sweep_expired` deadlock.

`place_hold` calls `reserve` before `Instant::now() + ttl`. `Instant + Duration` panics when the deadline does not fit. The panic unwinds after the reservation is committed and before the hold is inserted, so those units stay reserved with no hold id.

`confirm` `remove`s the hold before `release` or `ship`. If `ship` then returns `Insufficient` (reservations were cleared or over-released), the hold is gone and the remaining reservation cannot be confirmed or swept.

ISSUES:
L47: available computes on_hand - reserved and panics or wraps when reserved > on_hand
L81: receive overwrites an existing SKU, dropping on-hand quantity and reservations instead of adding qty
L101: release returns Ok and saturates when qty exceeds reserved
L112: ship subtracts qty from on_hand with no on_hand check, so it underflows when on_hand < qty
L120: record_loss subtracts lost from on_hand with no check and can leave reserved above on_hand
L127: total_value overflows u64 on the per-item multiply or on the sum
L144: moving_average panics when window is 0
L157: deltas reads prices[i + 1] for i in 0..len, so any non-empty slice panics
L157: deltas subtracts i64 prices with no overflow check
L185: lookup uses get_unchecked on an untrusted slot; an out-of-range index is undefined behavior
L196: append_batch dereferences a buf pointer after extend_from_slice may reallocate (use-after-free, undefined behavior)
L204: encode stores name.len() as u8, so names longer than 255 bytes produce a corrupt frame
L218: decode uses from_utf8_unchecked on network bytes; invalid UTF-8 is undefined behavior
L253: Instant::now() + ttl panics on overflow after reserve has already committed, leaking the reservation
L259: confirm locks holds then warehouse while place_hold and sweep_expired lock warehouse then holds, so they deadlock
L260: confirm removes the hold before release or ship; a later error leaves reserved units with no hold id

I am reviewing the Rust inventory service module for real defects. I will check for logic errors, panics, integer overflow, undefined behavior, memory safety issues, and concurrency problems.

`Item::available()` subtracts `reserved` from `on_hand`. If reserved exceeds on_hand, this panics in debug mode or wraps in release mode. I am checking whether the code can actually leave reserved larger than on_hand.

`record_loss` subtracts from `on_hand` without checking `reserved`. This can leave `reserved` larger than `on_hand`, causing `available()` to underflow. `receive` resets `reserved` to zero when replacing an item, which is a logic bug but does not directly cause the overflow. `release` silently allows releasing more than reserved because it uses saturating subtraction.

`ship` can underflow `on_hand` after `record_loss` leaves `reserved` larger than `on_hand`. `receive` replaces existing items with `insert`, which contradicts its documentation that it adds units to current stock.

`reserve` calls `item.available()` to check stock. If `record_loss` left `reserved` larger than `on_hand`, this call panics before the quantity check. The code then adds the requested quantity to `reserved` without verifying it fits within `u32`.

In release mode, `available()` can wrap to a huge value after `record_loss` leaves `reserved` larger than `on_hand`. The quantity check then passes, and adding the requested amount to `reserved` overflows `u32`.

`ship` subtracts `qty` from both `reserved` and `on_hand` without first verifying that `on_hand` is large enough. `record_loss` also subtracts `lost` from `on_hand` without checking that the loss does not exceed current stock.

`total_value` multiplies `on_hand` by `price_cents` and sums the results. This can overflow in both directions. `low_stock` calls `available()` during sorting, which can panic.

`moving_average` panics via `assert!` when the window is zero. This is a library panic on invalid input.

`deltas` panics on any non-empty price slice because its loop runs to `prices.len()` while indexing `prices[i + 1]`. The subtraction `prices[i + 1] - prices[i]` can also overflow `i64`.

`SlotTable::lookup` uses `get_unchecked` on an untrusted slot index from a handheld scanner. This is undefined behavior if the slot is out of bounds.

`append_batch` stores a raw pointer from `buf.as_ptr()` and later dereferences it after `extend_from_slice` may reallocate the buffer. This is use-after-free undefined behavior.

`encode` truncates the item name length to `u8`, so names longer than 255 bytes are silently cut off and cannot be decoded back correctly.

`decode` uses `from_utf8_unchecked` on untrusted network bytes. Invalid UTF-8 triggers undefined behavior.

`decode` should use `from_utf8` and return a `Malformed` error instead of `from_utf8_unchecked`. The length arithmetic in `decode` is safe. I am now examining `place_hold` for lock ordering problems.

`place_hold` acquires the warehouse lock before the holds and next_id locks. `confirm` acquires the holds lock before the warehouse lock. This reversed ordering creates a deadlock risk between those two functions.

`sweep_expired` acquires the warehouse lock before the holds lock. This completes the AB-BA deadlock cycle with `confirm`, which holds holds while waiting for warehouse. `confirm` also holds the holds lock while calling release and ship, which need warehouse; if sweep holds warehouse and waits for holds, a second deadlock is possible.

The `next_id` counter is a `u64`, so incrementing it past `2^64` would overflow. This is practically impossible and will be skipped.

A logic race exists between `confirm` and `sweep_expired`. `confirm` removes a hold while holding the `holds` lock, then releases warehouse stock before dropping that lock. If `sweep_expired` acquires the warehouse lock first, it can see the hold and attempt to release its stock, but the hold is already gone. This creates a double-release or inconsistent state.

`place_hold` computes `expires: Instant::now() + ttl`. If the TTL is large enough, this addition panics because `Instant` does not overflow. The code should use `checked_add` instead.

The `Instant::now() + ttl` addition can panic after `reserve` already committed stock. The reservation leaks because the warehouse mutation persists while the hold is never inserted.

`moving_average` sums `u32` price deltas into a `u64`. If the window is large enough, the total can overflow `u64`.

`ship` is safe only if the `reserved <= on_hand` invariant holds. If `record_loss` or `release` corrupts that invariant, `ship` can underflow `on_hand`.

`confirm` removes the expired hold before calling `ship`. If `ship` fails, the hold is already gone and the reservation may remain orphaned.

The `confirm` hold-removal-before-ship failure is a minor transactional bug. The `Warehouse` is private to `Service`, so external callers cannot overwrite items and break the reservation invariant.

The `next_id` counter is incremented while holding the `holds` lock, so no two threads can race to assign the same ID.

`low_stock` is not a separate defect because it merely calls `available()`, which already panics on the same condition. The `moving_average` precision loss from large windows is too minor to list. The `assert!` in `moving_average` is a deliberate precondition check rather than an unguarded panic.

`append_batch` also violates Rust's aliasing rules. It stores a raw pointer from `buf.as_ptr()` while `extend_from_slice` mutably borrows the same buffer, creating a stacked-borrow violation.

<summary goes here>

`encode` computes `Vec::with_capacity(1 + name.len() + 8)`. If the item name is extremely long, this expression overflows `usize` and panics in debug or wraps silently in release.

`parse_command` returns borrowed `&str` slices from the input line, which is safe. `decode` silently discards trailing bytes when the buffer contains multiple records; this is acceptable because the function is documented to decode one record.

`release` decrements `reserved` without checking that the hold still exists or that the stock level is sufficient, so it can leave the reservation count negative. `receive` for an existing SKU violates the specification by overwriting the item rather than adding to its stock.

The `reserved += qty` overflow is not a real defect because `available()` already bounds the quantity to `on_hand - reserved`, so the sum cannot exceed `u32::MAX`. The lock ordering between `confirm` and `sweep_expired` does not create a deadlock; the held locks prevent any conflicting access.

`deltas` pre-allocates `prices.len() - 1` elements but pushes `prices.len()` items, so the final push panics on an out-of-bounds index. The `SlotTable::lookup` method returns a copied `Option` via unsafe code.

`SlotTable::lookup` uses `get_unchecked` on an untrusted slot index. This is undefined behavior when the index is out of bounds, and it can read unmapped memory.

The wire format intentionally omits reserved and price fields, so that is not a defect. The receive log always prints "receive" even when replacing an existing SKU, which is a minor quirk tied to the replace bug. HashMap iteration order in total_value does not matter for correctness because addition is commutative; any overflow would still be caused by the underlying arithmetic.

`Instant` is safe to use for TTL within a single process, so the hold expiration logic is sound. `Service` does not implement `Clone`, which is acceptable.

`release` can underflow `reserved` when the hold is missing or the quantity exceeds the reservation. It returns `Ok` and `Expired`, which leaves the reservation at zero and may release stock that belongs to other holds.

`ship` does not verify that `on_hand >= qty`, so it can panic when the stock level is too low. The `available()` subtraction underflow at line 47, the `record_loss` reservation corruption at line 120, and the `ship` underflow at line 112 are distinct panic sites that all stem from the same broken invariant.

I am now separating critical bugs from weaker issues. The must-fix list includes receive data loss, record_loss underflow, available and ship underflows, the deltas out-of-bounds panic, the SlotTable unsafe lookup, and the Instant overflow in place_hold.

`confirm` does not deadlock on itself because `wh.release` borrows the existing `MutexGuard<Warehouse>` rather than re-locking. Receiving an existing SKU while it is reserved overwrites the old item with zero reserved stock and the new quantity, so subsequent holds or ships will fail or ship the wrong stock.

Rust integer overflow panics in debug builds and wraps silently in release, so it is a real defect distinct from undefined behavior. The `Vec::as_ptr` plus `extend_from_slice` pattern in `append_batch` is confirmed as a textbook use-after-free.

The `moving_average` overflow is not a real defect. A slice large enough to overflow `u64` would require more elements than can fit in memory, so the panic cannot occur.

The `moving_average` sum can overflow `u64` when the window contains more than `2^32` elements, because `2^32 * u32::MAX` exceeds `2^64`. This is a real integer-overflow defect.

The `moving_average` assertion against a zero window is a one-line defect. The large-window sum overflow and the `usize` capacity overflow are too theoretical to include.

The lock ordering in `confirm` is the root cause of the deadlock. Locking warehouse before holds would make hold removal and shipping atomic with respect to `sweep_expired`. Mutexes already prevent data races.

SlotTable is not thread-safe. It contains a Vec and has no interior synchronization, so concurrent lookups and mutations would race unless the caller provides external locks.

`append_batch` is single-threaded, so its use-after-free is sequential undefined behavior rather than a concurrency bug. In `place_hold`, if the holds lock is acquired after the warehouse reservation is already taken and then `Instant::now() + ttl` panics, the reservation leaks because the guard drops while the hold is missing. The review will open with a summary of the most serious issues.

I will cite L196 for the `append_batch` use-after-free and L204 for the `encode` name truncation. The `deltas` out-of-bounds panic and `moving_average` overflow will both be listed at L157. I am also weighing whether to include the silent saturating arithmetic in `release` as a separate issue.

I will include the silent saturating arithmetic in `release` as a separate defect. It is inconsistent and wrong: over-release succeeds.

The `decode` unwrap is safe because the preceding length check guarantees the slice has exactly four bytes. The `Warehouse.receive` replace bug also overwrites the item's price when adding stock to an existing SKU.

The `receive` comment claims existing SKUs only add units, but the code overwrites name and price. Receiving an existing SKU also resets `reserved` to zero, so any active holds become stale and later confirmations or ships will fail with `Insufficient`.

The hold is removed before the ship attempt, so a failed ship leaves the reservation zeroed and the hold deleted. This makes the failure messy rather than a clean orphaned reservation. The interaction between receive overwriting reserved stock and confirm removing holds before shipping is a cross-function logic bug that will be described under both functions.

A failed ship in `confirm` leaves a permanent reservation leak. The hold is removed before shipping, so if the ship fails, the units stay reserved and there is no hold ID to release them later. This occurs when `reserved` is too low, which happens if `receive` overwrote the item and zeroed its reserved stock, or if `release` used saturating subtraction on an oversized quantity.

`record_loss` does not reduce `reserved`, so a later `ship` can pass the `reserved` check and then panic on `on_hand`. Because `sweep_expired` and `place_hold` manage reservations exactly, the total held quantity should equal `reserved` under normal use. This means the `ship` panic is only reachable if `reserved` was corrupted by an external write or by `release` saturating.

The `confirm` hold-removal-before-ship pattern is a realistic Service bug. If `ship` fails, the reservation stays leaked and the hold vanishes. The expired path is also unsafe: `saturating_sub` in `release` can return `Ok` while failing to restore all stock, leaving the hold gone and the reservation zeroed.

`decode` uses `from_utf8_unchecked`, so invalid UTF-8 from the network triggers undefined behavior.

The `confirm` deadlock is caused by `confirm` acquiring the holds lock before the warehouse lock, while `place_hold` and `sweep_expired` acquire the warehouse lock first. I will keep the `moving_average` zero-window panic and the silent saturating `release` as separate issues.

The `append_batch` use-after-free is worsened by the fact that the head value is already a `Copy` type, so the unsafe pointer read is unnecessary. The `lookup` function at line 185 uses `get_unchecked` on an untrusted slot index, which turns scanner input into a direct out-of-bounds read.

The `sweep_expired` closure is memory-safe. It only borrows each hold immutably and never mutates the holds vector, so `retain` cannot create aliasing or use-after-free bugs.

`record_loss` has two distinct bugs. It panics immediately when the loss exceeds `on_hand`. When the loss is smaller but still larger than `available`, it succeeds and silently breaks the invariant, which later causes `ship` to panic.

In release mode, `record_loss` with a loss exceeding `on_hand` wraps the count to a huge number, leaves `reserved` unchanged, and causes `total_value` to overflow. The deadlock occurs when one thread holds the warehouse lock while another holds the holds lock; `place_hold` widens this window because it acquires the warehouse lock before the holds lock.

The review now totals 16 distinct real defects. The `moving_average` zero-window panic is a documented precondition contract rather than an implementation bug.

A name longer than 255 bytes causes `encode` to write a truncated length prefix. `decode` then reads that many bytes as the name, but the remaining buffer is still long enough for a full record, so it returns `Ok` with silently corrupted data.

The `decode` unchecked UTF-8 read is undefined behavior when the truncated length prefix lands inside a multi-byte character, not merely silent corruption. A valid UTF-8 string can be cut at an arbitrary byte boundary and still be invalid UTF-8.
